1. Introduction to Jurassic English™ Level 2
1.1
Mission
Statement:
The
Architecture
of
Causality
At Level 2: Development, the intellectual mission transitions from foundational identiﬁcation to structural
connection. For learners aged 8–10, language is no longer merely a system for naming the world; it becomes
the primary engine for analyzing Causality. We aim to move learners across the A1 →  A2 threshold by shifting
their focus from what is happening to why it is happening. We operate on the central premise: If
X
happens,
then
Y
feels
Z.
1.2
Pedagogical
Positioning:
The
Transition
to
Textual
Evidence
Level 2 occupies the crucial bridge between early literacy (Pre-A1/A1) and intermediate reasoning (B1). While
Level 1 focused on physiological regulation and oral claims, Level 2 introduces Scaﬀolded
Written
CEIW
(Claim, Evidence, Interpretation, Warrant) and Student-Initiated
Regulation. The "weight" of the reasoning
transfers from the teacher's prompts to the student's written documentation of textual evidence.
1.3
Standards
Alignment:
CEFR
A1
 → 
A2
&
CCSS
Anchors
Level 2 is meticulously mapped to international standards, ensuring that cognitive development and linguistic
acquisition occur simultaneously.

1.4
Core
Cognitive
Progression:
The
Causality
Engine
The Development level advances the "Stratigraphy of Cognition" through a four-step evolutionary jump tailored
for the 8–10 age band:
1. Observation: Distinguishing between what the text explicitly states and what must be inferred.
2. Causality: Understanding the mechanical and emotional chain reactions within a narrative ("If X →  Y").
3. Application: Assessing the fairness, morality, or quality of a character's decision based on stated criteria.
4. Justiﬁcation: Constructing a formal argument where the Warrant explicitly explains why the evidence
supports the claim.

Publisher
Statement
World Wise Learning (WWL) recognizes Level 2 as the crucible of academic endurance. It is here that students
ﬁrst encounter the friction of putting complex thoughts onto paper. Failure to properly scaﬀold the CEIW
structure here leads to the "B1 Plateau" later. This manual provides the granular, step-by-step architecture
needed to ensure every Lesson 2 cycle develops rigorous, evidenced-based thinkers.

Level: Ages 8–10 (CEFR A1 →  A2)
Subject: English Language Arts (Jurassic English™ Level 2: Development)
Duration: 45 minutes
Overall
Learning
Goals
Students will open the Iron
Man dig site by distinguishing explicit text from inference. Ted Hughes's opening —
the Iron Man at the cliﬀ edge, the fall, the reassembly — is one of the most evocative passages in 20th-century
children's literature. Today's job: separate what the text actually
says from what the reader imagines and fears.
Speciﬁc
Learning
Objectives
1. Students will independently initiate the Butterﬂy Hug or Cool Down Pass.
2. Students will distinguish explicit textual statements from inferred meaning in Chapter 1 of The
Iron
Man.
3. Students will locate, highlight (blue), and cite (page + paragraph) at least three pieces of explicit evidence
about the Iron Man's appearance and arrival.
4. Students will pass the Parrot Eﬀect Check by orally interpreting cited evidence in their own words.

Diﬀerentiation
/
Accommodations
Neuroinclusive
(Dyslexia): Audio runs the entire Phase 2. During Phase 3, pair the student with a peer who
reads the target paragraph aloud while the dyslexic student locates the highlight. Pre-chunked text version
available.
Neuroinclusive
(ADHD): Use Phase 3 as a movement break — student walks to a posted version of the
chapter on the wall and highlights there. Chunk the three Claims into one at a time.
Neuroinclusive
(Anxiety): Strict No Cold Call. Whisper-prompt the page in advance. Allow the student to
write the citation on a Post-it instead of speaking it.
